audit.why: EVEN at 5.5/10 with 51.31% over 191 games. Barrel Roll pokes from 850 against a 650 charge, but neither champion kills the other through Frost Armor and Drunken Rage, so the lane is a poke-and-farm standoff that resolves in teamfights.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike is described qualitatively — 'his W damage reduction', 'his Body Slam E kite' — with no cooldown attached to any of them, so none of them tells you when to act.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s at 600 range and is both his engage and his escape; Barrel Roll is 10/9/8/7/6s at 850; Drunken Rage is 5s flat; Explosive Cask is 100/85/70s. Against Arctic Assault's 18s, Body Slam comes back faster than your engage does — which is why the advice has to be to go when his E is spent, not merely 'when he oversteps'.
audit.corrected: Body Slam's 14s and Barrel Roll's 850 range written into whys[0], whys[2], the cooldown block and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (a) Drunken Rage is never named — it is called 'W damage reduction' five times — and its auto-attack component is missing entirely. (b) 'drains your Fury of the North passive resistances' and 'passive armor stacks' describe Frost Armor as a depleting stack pool. (c) 'one landed comet' — Glacial Prison is a bola.
audit.why: Riot on Drunken Rage: 'Gragas samples his latest brew for 1 second. After finishing, he becomes boisterous and belligerent, dealing magic damage to all nearby enemies on his next basic attack and reducing damage received.' It is a 5-second empowered attack with damage reduction attached, and the drink animation is the tell — the wind-up is what you step back from, not the Body Slam. Riot on Fury of the North: Frost Armor grants armour, MR and slow immunity, and 'persists for a short time after Sejuani takes damage'. So poke does strip it, but by ending the out-of-combat state, not by grinding down stacks — and the fix is to break combat, which no amount of standing still will do while he pokes.
audit.corrected: Drunken Rage named with its 5-second empowered-attack behaviour; Frost Armor described as an out-of-combat buff that lapses shortly after you are hit; bola replaces comet.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns calls Body Slam matchup-defining and gives no number, then pads with a generic line about 'Q dash spent on poke'.
audit.why: Body Slam 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s, Barrel Roll 10/9/8/7/6s, Drunken Rage 5s, Arctic Assault 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s. His engage-escape returns faster than yours at every rank, which is the actual reason you never open the trade.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' names neither the heal nor the item.
audit.why: Happy Hour is his passive: 'Gragas periodically heals upon using a skill' — it is a per-ability heal, so it scales with how long the fight lasts, which is exactly the fight shape a Sejuani CC chain produces. Thornmail is already in the build path and carries Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: Thornmail named and tied to Happy Hour.

audit.why: The listed mistake pattern — engaging into a live Body Slam and burning Arctic Assault as a trade opener rather than an exit — is the right one and is not split by elo.

edits.after: Level 1 is a range problem — Barrel Roll pokes from 850 while your charge reaches 650, and Frost Armor lapses shortly after you take damage, so every barrel you stand in costs you the armour, MR and slow immunity it grants. Hug the wave edge and last-hit with W rather than stepping forward. At level 2 Drunken Rage arrives: a 1-second drink that reduces the damage he takes and empowers his next basic, so any Permafrost stun you land there costs you more than it costs him — hold the stun and concede the level-2 initiative. At level 3 your full combo is live: Q knock-up into both W arcs into Permafrost punishes him if you catch him flat-footed, but time it around Body Slam — 14 seconds at rank 1, and his escape as well as his engage.
edits.before: Level 1 is a genuine coin flip of range — Gragas's Q barrel poke drains your Fury of the North passive resistances if you stand in the puddle, so hug the wave edge and last-hit with W rather than stepping forward. At level 2 his W damage reduction absorbs your early trading damage, meaning any E Permafrost stun you land costs you more than it costs him — hold the stun and concede the level-2 initiative. At level 3 your full combo is live: Q-knock-up into W double-strike into E Permafrost stun is a punishing burst if you catch him flat-footed, but time it around his W cooldown — Body Slam E in with W active and he soaks the stun and fires back through your diminished HP.

edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are a Gragas control window — Happy Hour heals him on every ability while your Frost stacks only matter if you survive the barrel poke long enough to close. Play the wave: freeze near your tower lip to force him to overextend for CS, and only Q-engage when Body Slam is visibly on cooldown so he cannot reposition out of your Permafrost follow-up. At level 6 the dynamic shifts sharply — Glacial Prison is a 1300-range initiation he cannot dash away from, and one landed bola forces the full stun chain. Call for your jungler at 6; Explosive Cask can peel for him, but at 100 seconds, if it is already spent on a wave or a trade, the kill window is clean.

notes: The tell this page never gave the player: Drunken Rage is a 1-second drink animation, and Riot's text makes the empowered basic attack the payload. The moment to step back is the drink, not the Body Slam — by the time the E is cast the empowered auto is already loaded. That matches the autoreset-burst-tell row in _missing-interactions.json for this matchup. Second, the anti-heal row is genuine: Happy Hour heals on every ability cast, so a long CC-chain fight is the fight shape that feeds him most, and Thornmail is already on the build path. Third, the recurring Sejuani-wide error appears again in a new form — 'drains your Fury of the North passive resistances' and 'your Fury of the North passive armor stacks' treat Frost Armor as a depleting stack pool. It is not: it is granted for being out of combat and persists only briefly after she is hit. And 'comet' for Glacial Prison shows up again; Riot calls it a bola.
